Hi Daniel / NetWay ops team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap + items we discussed and outstanding asks so we can scope the private deployment and SLO validation window.

Summary of requirements you called out:
- Target tail latency (application-level): prefer 99th <= 120ms for short requests (<= 256 tokens) when hitting hosted model variant; fallback model ok up to 250ms.
- Sustained throughput target: 2k tokens/sec (approx ~65 RPS of ~30-token responses) during regular traffic, with 2× headroom for bursts.
- Concurrency: expected steady concurrency 150–300 active connections; burst up to ~400 concurrent streams for short windows.
- Streaming: support chunked token streaming with per-chunk delivery; prefer sub-80ms per-chunk median within same region.
- Network: GCP us-west1 peering / Cloud VPN; egress through NAT IP(s) (please confirm exact addresses).

Outstanding asks from our side (items we need from NetWay to run the lab):
1) Confirm egress IP ranges or static NAT IP(s) we should expect for the test window.
2) Confirm VPN capacity and any enforced throttles (max throughput observed historically).
3) Provide a 30-minute pcap capture from a peak window (sample of the UDP/TCP flows) or allow us to run a client-side probe during the window. See attached sample-pcap-ask.txt for capture hints.
4) Any firewall/NAT timeouts we should know about (TCP keepalive settings, idle close).
5) Preferred test dates (we proposed Sept 22–23) and a technical contact for firewall/VPN changes.

Attached: NetWay_acceptance-test-plan_v1.pdf (draft acceptance criteria and test steps).

Next steps we propose:
- Karthik will confirm the test plan and pre-populate expected IPs for the lab.
- Camila will schedule a 60-minute lab slot with NetWay network and ops.
- Jonas will prepare a quantized fallback model configuration for degraded bandwidth testing.

If this matches your recollection, please reply with the egress IPs and a contact for the VPN folks so we can finalize the runbook.

Thanks,

--
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Daniel — helpful details. A few operational notes from our side and proposed acceptance criteria for the lab run: 

Operational notes:
- We'll run three phases during the lab: baseline (low traffic), sustained load, and burst/failure injection (throttle VPN to observe graceful degradation).
- We'll need a short firewall rule change that allows our test runner to open outbound TLS to the Redwood control endpoint from your test host (the control channel is outbound-only; no inbound rules required).
- Please provide the exact NAT IP(s) before the run so we can filter telemetry and attribute pcap samples.

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Phase A (baseline): median token latency <= 40ms, 95th <= 80ms.
- Phase B (sustained): sustained token throughput >= 2k tokens/s, 99th token latency <= 220ms.
- Phase C (burst / constrained): system maintains availability with graceful fallback (quantized model) and request success rate >= 98% for up to 10 minutes of throttling.

Attachments: NetWay_acceptance-test-plan_v1.pdf (updated draft), sample-pcap-ask.txt

Action items: 
- Karthik: confirm NetWay NAT IP(s and CIDRs).
- Camila: propose 2 x 60 minute windows (Sept 22 local morning, Sept 23 afternoon) for runbook + test.
- Jonas: prep quantized fallback model and load profile.
